reason: I tried to break the wording and the lineation and failed at both, then broke the locator instead. On wording and lineation the verifier is vindicated by better evidence than it had. I downloaded the hOCR of the very scan it names, Internet Archive fireflies0000tago (Tagore, Fireflies, New York: Macmillan, 1928, decorations by Artzybasheff, published February 1928), and read its line boxes. The piece is grouped as two ocr_line runs: line one “The butterfly counts not months but moments,” and line two “and has time enough.” So the break after moments is the edition's, the lower case and at the head of line two is the edition's, and the terminal stop is there. A second, independent scan, Internet Archive dli.venugopal.844 of the same Macmillan setting, breaks it in the same place. No translator is owed: Tagore made Fireflies in English, so there is no drift to hunt. Shipped.js clean, Tagore 0 of 3, not banned, 1928 so in scope, nothing needing a warning, tag Poetry right, source line 71 characters, leads with the name, no dash. What fails is rule 4. It requires a LOCATABLE citation, and where a work has no books, chapters, letters or numbered sections it requires edition and page. Fireflies in this edition numbers no pieces; “the butterfly couplet” is a description, not a locator, and it is a slightly wrong one, since the piece is an unrhymed two line poem and not a couplet. The page was there to be had and the verifier did not take it. From the same hOCR, the page numbers sit at the foot of each page: “[14]” closes the Mind's underground moths piece, the butterfly piece follows, and “[15]” closes it. The butterfly is page 15. The dli scan agrees, its OCR losing only the [15] and [16] markers. So this is refuted as written and entirely repairable: ship it with the page. The quotation, the two line form and the edition all stand exactly as proposed.
